instruction.text: What are personal boundaries? Fill in the gaps.

atoms.b: Personal boundaries are the ((++limits homework)) and rules we set for ourselves in our relationships. These are ((++different the_same)) for everyone.
You should ((++communicate ignore)) your personal boundaries to others to make sure they do not make you ((++uncomfortable happy)).

instruction.text: There are many different kinds of personal boundaries. Match the types of boundaries to their definitions.

hint.text: These are just three examples of how personal boundaries can be categorised, but your personal boundaries don’t have to fit into a specific category. What matters is that you know what you are okay and not okay with.

atoms.b: how physically close people can get to you and how much physical contact is allowed
atoms.sound: physical boundaries are how physically close people can get to you and how much physical contact is allowed

atoms.b: how much emotional energy you have for other people
atoms.sound: emotional boundaries are how much emotional energy you have for other people.

atoms.b: what you are comfortable and not comfortable with when people talk to you
atoms.sound: verbal boundaries are what you are comfortable and not comfortable with when people talk to you

instruction.text: Read the text about each person’s personal boundaries and decide what actions are okay and not okay with them.

atoms.text: Amirah likes hugging and holding hands with her female friends, but only when they ask her first. She does not like being touched or hugged without warning. She is also not comfortable with hugs or touches from boys.

atoms.a: Amirah’s best friend hugging her from behind as a surprise
Amirah’s friend holding hands with her after asking her first
a boy from Amirah’s class trying to play with her hair

instruction.text: Read the text about each person’s personal boundaries and decide what actions are okay and not okay with them.

atoms.text: When Bradley is having a bad day, he prefers to keep to himself. He likes having time alone and doesn’t like to be bothered by others. He feels uncomfortable when people try to make him talk about it.

atoms.a: Bradley’s friends gathering around him and trying to make him laugh
Bradley’s friends asking him lots of questions about why he looks upset
Bradley’s friends telling him that they are there for him if he needs them, but they will give him space for now

instruction.text: Read the text about each person’s personal boundaries and decide what actions are okay and not okay with them.

atoms.text: Poppy is a very good listener. However, she is uncomfortable with having to keep so many people’s secrets. She also finds it very stressful when her friends expect her to always have the time to listen to them.

atoms.a: Poppy’s friend asking if she has the time and energy first before sharing their problems with her
Poppy’s friend respecting it if she doesn’t want to hear and have to keep their secret
Poppy’s friend telling her to stay and talk when she is busy or not in the mood

instruction.text: How should you communicate your personal boundaries? Read the conversation between Theo and Sofia and fill in the gaps with the correct words.

feedback.finish:
You should clearly let your friends know what you are okay or not okay with, but make sure to be patient and understanding. They often might not realise that their actions are crossing your personal boundaries.

However, if they don’t want to listen or change their behaviour, you should think about how much of a true friend they really are.

atoms.b: Hi, Sofia. Can I talk to you about something?
atoms.sound: ssml: <prosody pitch = '+0.5st'> Hi Sofia. Can I talk to you about something?</prosody>

atoms.b: Of course! What do you want to ((++talk cry)) about?
atoms.sound: ssml: <prosody pitch = '+1st'> Of course, what do you want to talk about?</prosody>

atoms.b: I want you to know that it makes me feel a little ((++tired relaxed)) when you ask me to play after school all the time. I’m not always in the ((++mood car)).
atoms.sound: ssml: <prosody pitch = '+0.5st'> I want you to know that it makes me feel a little tired when you ask me to play after school all the time. I’m not always in the mood.</prosody>

atoms.b: I didn’t realise, but ((++thanks sorry)) for telling me! What should I do instead?
atoms.sound: ssml: <prosody pitch = '+1st'> I didn’t realise, but thanks for telling me! What should I do instead?</prosody>

atoms.b: It'd make me feel better if you ((++ask beg)) me first if I actually want to play, and not try to change my mind if I say ((++no yes)).
atoms.sound: ssml: <prosody pitch = '+0.5st'> It'd make me feel better if you ask me first if I actually want to play, and not try to change my mind if I say no.</prosody>

atoms.b: Okay, I’ll ((++do ignore)) that from now on. I’m sorry if I’ve been making you ((++sad happy)).
atoms.sound: ssml: <prosody pitch = '+1st'> Okay, I’ll do that from now on. I’m sorry if I’ve been making you sad.</prosody>

atoms.b: It’s okay, you didn’t know how it makes me ((++feel sing)), so I wanted to talk to you about it. Thanks for hearing me out!
atoms.sound: ssml: <prosody pitch = '+0.5st'> It’s okay, you didn’t know how it makes me feel, so I wanted to talk to you about it. Thanks for hearing me out!</prosody>
